question: Litolff page 4, one mark (padded box pointing at a small mark hanging from the top staff line). Is that mark a dot that belongs to the note just left of it?
verbatim: Those dots are Stacatto markings and belong to the note underneath it
ours: He names the dots in the tile as staccato marks, each belonging to the note beneath it -- so nothing in this tile is a dot that lengthens a note, and the dotted reading the rule made here is wrong. Whether he meant the small bump inside the box or the round dots above the staff is not clear from the words; asked.

follow_up.asked: Is the small bump under the top staff line, inside the box, anything at all, or a flaw in the print?
follow_up.verbatim: IT is actually a Stacatto mark
follow_up.ours: The boxed mark itself is a staccato dot, printed touching the staff line; with his first answer, it belongs to the note underneath it (the note it stands above), not to the note on its left.
